testingRequirements: Tests must validate user-facing behavior, not implementation details
Focus on what users actually do - integration tests over unit tests
Don't mock excessively - test real behavior where possible
Coverage metrics are meaningless - user flow coverage is everything

userStories.title: Centralize verification lifecycle orchestration behind one core interface
acceptanceCriteria: There is one externally used core interface for running/settling verification; queue worker and CLI do not duplicate status-transition SQL.
No adapter can mark verification passed, write verification evidence, or loop a ticket back without going through the lifecycle interface.
Tests cover identical lifecycle behavior through CLI/debug and worker call paths.
The extracted modules reduce coupling without changing the verification audit format or current UI/API behavior.
userStories.description:
## Why
The verification gate is becoming the deepest workflow in Brain Dump: it boots apps, executes step specs, writes evidence, persists audit rows, files findings, changes ticket status, syncs PRD state, and triggers epic auto-PR. Today most of that lives inside core/verification.ts. Adding a queue worker, CLI/debug commands, and UI status reads without a deliberate seam risks duplicating transition and evidence rules across adapters.

## Scope
1. Define one core verification lifecycle interface that owns the durable state transition from ai_verification to done, in_progress, or blocked ai_verification.
2. Keep adapters thin: CLI run/debug commands, the automatic worker, future MCP read tools, and UI/server functions must call the lifecycle/read interfaces instead of issuing their own verification SQL or status transitions.
3. Split implementation internals only where they buy locality: boot/discovery, step executors, evidence/report writing, queue/job coordination, and epic completion can be internal modules behind the same lifecycle interface.
4. Preserve current semantics exactly: certified pass completes, assertion failure files findings and loops back, infra_error/uncertified blocks loudly, PRD sync and epic auto-PR happen only through the lifecycle.
5. Add tests proving CLI/manual debug and worker execution produce the same persisted run, comments, findings, PRD updates, and ticket status for pass, fail, infra_error, and uncertified outcomes.
6. Add an architecture note documenting the interface invariants and the adapters that are allowed to cross this seam.

## Acceptance criteria
- There is one externally used core interface for running/settling verification; queue worker and CLI do not duplicate status-transition SQL.
- No adapter can mark verification passed, write verification evidence, or loop a ticket back without going through the lifecycle interface.
- Tests cover identical lifecycle behavior through CLI/debug and worker call paths.
- The extracted modules reduce coupling without changing the verification audit format or current UI/API behavior.

userStories.title: Extract reusable durable job leasing for verification and epic review queues
acceptanceCriteria: Verification queue leasing reuses a shared core implementation or an explicitly documented shared pattern, not copy-pasted SQL.
Concurrent workers cannot run the same ticket verification job.
Expired running jobs recover deterministically after restart.
Tests cover claim/retry/dead-letter behavior and prove enqueue remains cheap.
userStories.description:
## Why
The codebase already has queue-shaped state for focused epic review runs (epic_review_runs and epic_review_run_tickets), and the AI Verification Gate now needs durable queued/running/retry/dead-letter behavior too. Implementing a second bespoke lease/retry model would duplicate fragile concurrency logic and make stalled jobs harder to reason about.

## Scope
1. Audit existing epic review run queue behavior and the planned verification queue requirements.
2. Extract or codify a shared durable job/lease helper in core for claim, heartbeat/lease expiry, complete, fail/retry, dead-letter, and stale-running recovery.
3. Apply the helper to the verification queue, and either adapt epic review run ticket leasing to it or document a concrete reason it must remain separate.
4. Keep SQLite writes narrow and indexed; no polling or lease recovery work in route loaders, MCP dispatch, or app startup hot paths.
5. Include race tests for two workers claiming the same job, expired lease recovery, idempotent enqueue, retry backoff, and dead-letter state.
6. Expose the minimal read model needed by UI/CLI without leaking mutation methods to implementing agents.

## Acceptance criteria
- Verification queue leasing reuses a shared core implementation or an explicitly documented shared pattern, not copy-pasted SQL.
- Concurrent workers cannot run the same ticket verification job.
- Expired running jobs recover deterministically after restart.
- Tests cover claim/retry/dead-letter behavior and prove enqueue remains cheap.

userStories.title: Gate generated verification plans against acceptance-criteria coverage
acceptanceCriteria: A ticket cannot enter ai_verification with executable steps that leave acceptance criteria uncovered without a loud rationale.
Verification reports show criterion-to-step coverage for every run.
Existing legacy demo scripts remain readable, but regenerated handoffs must satisfy the coverage gate.
Tests prove shallow smoke checks are rejected when they do not cover the ticket's acceptance criteria.
userStories.description:
## Why
Executable demo steps prevent fake manual approval, but they do not guarantee the steps prove the ticket. An agent can still generate a shallow check such as loading a page title while the real acceptance criteria remain unverified. The epic needs a verification-plan quality gate so automation maps to the ticket's actual requirements.

## Scope
1. Extend demo generation validation so each acceptance criterion/subtask is covered by at least one executable verification step, or has an explicit non-certifiable rationale that keeps the ticket from certified completion.
2. Add stable coverage references to DemoStep or demo script metadata so run reports can show which criteria each step proves.
3. Reject new ai_verification handoffs when coverage is missing, vague, or manual-only for criteria that can be automated.
4. Update Ralph prompts/tool descriptions so agents author coverage-aware steps for UI, API, command, and file automation.
5. Surface coverage in the verification panel/report so reviewers can audit what was and was not proven.
6. Add tests for tickets with subtasks, markdown acceptance criteria, regenerated demos after loop-back, and shallow/vague automation attempts.

## Acceptance criteria
- A ticket cannot enter ai_verification with executable steps that leave acceptance criteria uncovered without a loud rationale.
- Verification reports show criterion-to-step coverage for every run.
- Existing legacy demo scripts remain readable, but regenerated handoffs must satisfy the coverage gate.
- Tests prove shallow smoke checks are rejected when they do not cover the ticket's acceptance criteria.

userStories.title: Define command and file automation safety policy before execution
acceptanceCriteria: Unsafe command/file automation is rejected before execution with actionable errors.
Runtime execution enforces the same policy as generate-demo validation.
Evidence and findings cannot leak common secret/token environment values.
Tests cover injection, traversal, symlink, timeout, output cap, and redaction cases.
userStories.description:
## Scope note (2026-07-06 epic audit)
Command/file automation execution already shipped in tickets 36f2306d and 68ecfac3 (commits fd32c95..bc4185f) before this policy ticket ran. This ticket is now a RETROACTIVE AUDIT + HARDENING pass: audit the shipped executor in core/verification.ts against the policy below, close any gaps, and encode the policy as executable checks/tests rather than a design doc. The title's "before execution" framing is obsolete.

## Why
Command and file automation are necessary for docs, prompt generation, and validation tickets, but they also create an AI-authored execution surface. argv arrays and project-scoped paths are necessary but not sufficient: the runner needs an explicit safety policy before it executes commands or reads files as certification evidence.

## Scope
1. Define a core safety policy for command/file automation: allowed command categories, denylisted binaries/flags, project-scoped cwd, path normalization, timeout, output/file size caps, and no shell interpolation.
2. Strip or explicitly allow environment variables for command steps; redact secrets/tokens from stdout, stderr, manifests, evidence JSON, and verification findings.
3. Add per-project trust/config controls for enabling command automation, with a safe default for untrusted or missing config.
4. Route schema validation and executor enforcement through the same policy module so validation and runtime behavior cannot drift.
5. Record policy decisions in evidence: accepted command metadata, rejected reason, timeout/kill details, and redaction markers without leaking sensitive values.
6. Add adversarial tests for path traversal, symlink escapes, shell metacharacters, dangerous binaries, missing timeouts, oversized output/files, and secret redaction.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unsafe command/file automation is rejected before execution with actionable errors.
- Runtime execution enforces the same policy as generate-demo validation.
- Evidence and findings cannot leak common secret/token environment values.
- Tests cover injection, traversal, symlink, timeout, output cap, and redaction cases.

userStories.title: Define automatic verifier identity and evidence attribution
acceptanceCriteria: Automatic worker verification reports are attributed to the correct provider-qualified Ralph identity when provider data exists.
Unknown attribution is visible and diagnostic, not silently treated as normal.
Comments, attachments, manifests, telemetry, and UI run history agree on the verifier identity for a run.
Tests cover provider inference, legacy repair, regenerated demos, and missing-provider fallback.
userStories.description:
## Scope note (2026-07-06 epic audit)
The verification queue, automatic worker (embedded in the app server, src/lib/db.ts startup), and evidence storage already shipped (tickets 8ec01ace, dca5c6f8, 7ea6f80f). This ticket is now a RETROACTIVE AUDIT + COMPLETION pass over the shipped attribution path. Known real-world gap observed 2026-07-06: worker-executed runs attribute evidence with whatever provider the embedded worker infers, and a stale long-running dev server's worker can execute jobs with outdated code and identity - actor/provenance on jobs and runs must make that visible.

## Why
Manual CLI runs can pass --provider, but the automatic verification worker is supposed to remove the human from the loop. Without a provider/actor model for queued jobs, automatic evidence falls back to weak attribution such as unknown ralph, making the audit trail less useful and breaking the epic's provider-qualified evidence goal.

## Scope
1. Define the verifier identity model for automatic jobs: actor, provider, source surface, and fallback behavior when provider cannot be inferred.
2. Store provider/actor on verification jobs and verification runs, and include it in manifests, verification_report comments, attachment uploaders, telemetry, and UI run history.
3. Establish provider source precedence: explicit launch/review profile, active Ralph/session metadata, ticket branch/session telemetry, environment, then a loud unknown fallback.
4. Ensure repair-legacy-handoff and regenerated demos create jobs with preserved or recomputed attribution.
5. Update tests so worker-run evidence is attributed consistently across comments, attachments, manifests, and run history.
6. Document that implementing agents cannot choose attribution at evidence-write time; the runner resolves it from trusted workflow state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Automatic worker verification reports are attributed to the correct provider-qualified Ralph identity when provider data exists.
- Unknown attribution is visible and diagnostic, not silently treated as normal.
- Comments, attachments, manifests, telemetry, and UI run history agree on the verifier identity for a run.
- Tests cover provider inference, legacy repair, regenerated demos, and missing-provider fallback.

userStories.title: Consolidate verification evidence read model across UI, CLI, and MCP
acceptanceCriteria: Attachment/evidence normalization lives in one core read model rather than being copied in UI and MCP adapters.
UI, CLI, and MCP surfaces report the same verification evidence metadata and integrity state for a seeded run.
Missing/oversized/tampered evidence produces consistent, loud warnings without crashing the reader.
No evidence read adapter exposes write/pass/fail capabilities to implementing agents.
userStories.description:
## Why
Verification evidence is only valuable if every surface reads and presents the same artifact model. Today core writes evidence attachments, the UI/server attachment path builds its own read objects, and the MCP attachment loader has separate normalization/loading logic. As the automatic runner adds queue state, run history, reports, and failure context, duplicated evidence readers can drift on filenames, uploader normalization, size limits, image handling, and manifest integrity.

## Scope
1. Define a core read model for ticket attachments and verification evidence: metadata normalization, file lookup, MIME/type detection, safe size limits, evidence attachment resolution, and manifest integrity summary.
2. Move UI/server attachment reads, verification run history enrichment, CLI history output, and MCP attachment/context loading onto that read model or thin adapters over it.
3. Preserve adapter-specific presentation concerns only at the adapter layer: React image/lightbox rendering, MCP content blocks, CLI pretty output, and API response shapes.
4. Make missing evidence, oversized artifacts, tampered manifests, and legacy attachment metadata produce consistent warnings across surfaces.
5. Ensure evidence read paths remain read-only; no MCP/tool surface can write or mutate runner evidence.
6. Add tests that seed the same verification run/attachments and assert UI API, CLI history, and MCP context agree on evidence IDs, uploader, type, integrity, and warning behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Attachment/evidence normalization lives in one core read model rather than being copied in UI and MCP adapters.
- UI, CLI, and MCP surfaces report the same verification evidence metadata and integrity state for a seeded run.
- Missing/oversized/tampered evidence produces consistent, loud warnings without crashing the reader.
- No evidence read adapter exposes write/pass/fail capabilities to implementing agents.

userStories.title: Evidence storage with {provider} ralph attribution + consolidated verification report comment
acceptanceCriteria: Runner can attach screenshots/API captures + manifest and post one verification_report comment per run, all attributed "{provider} ralph"
Existing attachments with legacy uploadedBy values still render correctly
No new MCP surface allows evidence writes
userStories.description:
## Why
The attachment subsystem (tickets.attachments JSON + ~/.brain-dump/attachments/{ticketId}/, src/api/attachments.ts, src/lib/attachment-types.ts) already models AI uploaders — but the write path is browser-only (base64 over a TanStack server fn), and the uploader enum is a flat list (human/claude/ralph/opencode/cursor/copilot/codex/windsurf). Two requirements:
1. The runner (Node/core, not browser) must write evidence attachments directly.
2. Uploader attribution must be provider-qualified: **"{provider} ralph"** — claude ralph, pi ralph, cursor ralph, copilot ralph, codex ralph, opencode ralph — never bare "ralph".

## Scope
1. Core attachment write path: `core/attachments.ts` (or extend core/ticket.ts) — writeAttachmentFromFile(ticketId, filePath, metadata) storing into the same XDG attachments dir and appending to tickets.attachments with normalization shared with src/api/attachments.ts (move shared logic behind a core interface per architecture rules — no copying between adapters).
2. Provider-qualified uploader: replace the flat uploadedBy value for agent uploads with structured `{ agent: "ralph", provider: "claude" | "pi" | ... }` (or a validated template string, pick one and normalize legacy values on read). Detect provider via the existing environment-detection layer (src/lib/environment.ts + mcp-server/lib/environment.ts — note it is duplicated; keep both in sync or consolidate). Display name renders as "Claude Ralph", "Pi Ralph", etc. Extend comment-authors styling (src/lib/comment-authors.ts) so each provider-ralph combo gets the provider's color treatment.
3. New attachment types: `verification-screenshot`, `api-evidence`, `verification-manifest` added to AttachmentType (and the ticket tool's update-attachment enum).
4. Consolidated report: new comment type `verification_report` on ticket_comments — ONE comment per verification run, written directly by the runner through core (zero MCP calls, zero agent context burn): summary line, per-step verdict table, evidence attachment references, manifest integrity status. Author = "{provider} ralph".
5. Deliberately NO MCP action for uploading evidence or writing verification reports — agents must not be able to fabricate evidence. Document this as an invariant in the tool descriptions.
6. Tests: attachment write path, legacy uploader normalization, comment rendering of the new type (user-visible behavior).

## Acceptance criteria
- Runner can attach screenshots/API captures + manifest and post one verification_report comment per run, all attributed "{provider} ralph"
- Existing attachments with legacy uploadedBy values still render correctly
- No new MCP surface allows evidence writes

userStories.title: Verification failure loop-back into the Ralph iteration
acceptanceCriteria: A failed run automatically returns the ticket to in_progress with findings + evidence, and the next Ralph iteration's prompt contains the failure details
Passing rerun sets done; regressed steps re-fail correctly
Loop provably terminates: existing Ralph guards + the 3-strike blocked state; blocked tickets are visually flagged and excluded from further auto-iterations
userStories.description:
## Why
When verification fails, the implementation loop must restart automatically with the failure evidence in-context, and repeat until the runner reports clean — at which point the runner sets the ticket to done. The reject machinery already exists for rejection feedback (change_request comment → change-request-context.ts → generateEnhancedPRD "Fix This First" section) — verification failures reuse the same rails.

## Scope
1. On a failed run (from the runner's result object): file review_findings rows with a new category `verification` (severity from assertion criticality, default major), description containing the step, expected vs actual, and evidence attachment references; iteration tracked via ticket_workflow_state.review_iteration.
2. Transition ticket ai_verification → in_progress; keep PRD passes=false (core/prd-sync); reset demo step statuses for failed steps to failed with runner notes.
3. Context injection: extend src/lib/ralph-launch/change-request-context.ts (and src/api/context.ts equivalent) to also surface the latest failed verification report — a "Verification Failures — Fix This First" section in buildImplementationContext/buildReviewContext (src/api/ralph-prompts.ts) listing failed steps, assertions, and evidence file paths. Guard against stale reports the same way change requests are guarded (skip if a newer passing run exists).
4. Convergence rules:
   - Re-verification always re-runs ALL steps (a fix must not regress passing steps); previously failed steps are flagged in the new report.
   - verification findings must be marked fixed before generate-demo/re-verify can run (checkComplete already gates on open critical/major — ensure the new category counts).
   - Ralph's existing max-iterations and no-progress guards bound the loop; after 3 consecutive failed verification runs on the same step, STOP looping: leave the ticket in ai_verification with isBlocked=true and a blockedReason summarizing the stuck step + evidence refs, and post one needs-attention comment. This is the exception state that replaces the human gate — it must be loud on the board, not silent.
5. Completion trail: when the runner finally certifies and sets done, the ticket carries the full evidence trail (all runs, findings filed and fixed) so anyone can audit after the fact that issues found during verification were resolved without the ticket's scope suffering.
6. Integration tests: fail → finding filed → context contains failure section → pass on rerun → done. Test the 3-consecutive-failures blocked state and that Ralph's loop does not spin on a blocked ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- A failed run automatically returns the ticket to in_progress with findings + evidence, and the next Ralph iteration's prompt contains the failure details
- Passing rerun sets done; regressed steps re-fail correctly
- Loop provably terminates: existing Ralph guards + the 3-strike blocked state; blocked tickets are visually flagged and excluded from further auto-iterations

userStories.title: Evidence viewer UI: verification panel, run history, image rendering
acceptanceCriteria: A done ticket's modal/detail page shows per-step evidence, run history, and integrity status; a blocked ticket is unmistakable on the board and in the modal
Keyboard + ARIA on all new interactive elements
Bundle gates recorded (before/after numbers in completion summary per the perf runbook)
userStories.description:
## Why
There is no human approval step anymore, but the evidence must still be fully auditable after the fact: done tickets show proof, and blocked verification must be loud on the board. Today DemoPanel (src/components/tickets/DemoPanel.tsx) is a manual Pass/Fail checklist and Comment.tsx's markdown renderer cannot display images at all — evidence would be invisible.

## Scope
1. Replace the DemoPanel approval flow with a VerificationPanel (rename or evolve in place): per-step runner verdict with evidence — screenshot thumbnail (click → full-size lightbox with keyboard support: Esc close, focus trap — Rule 4) or API request/response viewer (method, URL, status pill, collapsible headers/body). No Pass/Fail buttons, no Approve/Request Changes — the runner decides; humans audit.
2. Verification run history: compact list of runs (status pill: passed/failed/uncertified/infra_error, git SHA, timestamp, duration), latest expanded. Integrity badge per run: manifest hash re-check (valid / tampered / uncertified-tripwire) with a tooltip explaining what it means.
3. Status-aware views: ai_verification → "verification pending/running/failed" live view (reuse the existing polling interval logic in ticket.$id.tsx); ai_verification + isBlocked → prominent needs-attention treatment (board card flag + panel banner with blockedReason and stuck-step evidence); done → read-only evidence trail.
4. Comment.tsx: verification_report comment type rendering (author chip "{Provider} Ralph" with provider color, verdict summary table, links to evidence); markdown renderer learns image support ONLY for attachment-served URLs (no arbitrary external images).
5. Attachment serving: evidence images served through the existing attachment read path; lazy-load thumbnails, no layout shift.
6. Performance: DemoPanel is already lazy-loaded — keep the lightbox/response-viewer inside that chunk; run pnpm build:analyze (bundle-sensitive: modal + route chunks) and pnpm test:e2e perf-renders if render counts change.
7. Tests (user behavior only): failed step shows screenshot + failure text; blocked ticket shows needs-attention banner with reason; integrity badge shows tampered state when manifest mismatch; done ticket shows full evidence trail.

## Acceptance criteria
- A done ticket's modal/detail page shows per-step evidence, run history, and integrity status; a blocked ticket is unmistakable on the board and in the modal
- Keyboard + ARIA on all new interactive elements
- Bundle gates recorded (before/after numbers in completion summary per the perf runbook)

userStories.title: End-to-end verification loop proof + docs across providers
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test passes in CI (pnpm check) and covers failure→repair→auto-done→epic-PR with zero human interaction
All workflow documentation shows the 6-status flow (backlog → ready → in_progress → ai_review → ai_verification → done); no stale human_review workflow references
doctor reports verification + PR capability status
userStories.description:
## Why
The epic's completion gate: prove the whole loop works end-to-end — including a forced failure, repair, auto-done, and epic auto-PR — and document the new flow everywhere agents and humans read about the workflow.

## Scope
1. Integration test (integration-tests/) driving a sample epic through the complete lifecycle: start-work → complete-work → ai_review findings → generate-demo with automation specs → verification run against a booted fixture app → forced assertion failure → loop-back (finding filed, status in_progress, context contains failure section) → fix → re-verify full suite passes → runner sets done with evidence + sealed manifest → last ticket done fires epic completion → PR created/readied automatically. Assert evidence files exist, manifest hashes validate, uploader is "{provider} ralph", exactly ONE verification_report comment exists per run, and no step required human input.
2. Tripwire test: a diff touching core/verification* produces an uncertified run that stays blocked in ai_verification (never reaches done).
3. Hook alignment: update enforce-review-before-push / provider hook equivalents (hooks/copilot/pre-tool-use.sh, .opencode/plugins/*) for the new flow (no human_review; verification gates instead); verify hooks don't block the runner's own operations or the epic auto-PR path.
4. Docs: update docs/universal-workflow.md, docs/claude-flow-ticket-lifecycle.md (Mermaid state diagram), docs/mcp-tools.md (submit-feedback removal/deprecation), docs/cli.md (verify command), docs/environments/*.md, CLAUDE.md status flow + quick reference. Provider skill files should already be regenerated via the sync script — verify no manual stragglers; grep for stale "human_review" workflow references.
5. brain-dump doctor: checks for Playwright availability, attachments dir writability, and gh auth (needed for epic auto-PR), with actionable remediation messages.

## Acceptance criteria
- Integration test passes in CI (pnpm check) and covers failure→repair→auto-done→epic-PR with zero human interaction
- All workflow documentation shows the 6-status flow (backlog → ready → in_progress → ai_review → ai_verification → done); no stale human_review workflow references
- doctor reports verification + PR capability status

## Worker-driven proof (merged from ticket 08427442)
The proof must also cover the automatic path, not just direct runner invocation:
1. Tickets handed to ai_verification are automatically queued, leased by the verification worker, run, repaired on failure, rerun, marked done, and finally trigger epic auto-PR creation WITHOUT anyone running `brain-dump verify`.
2. Drive the flow through the same public workflow/review APIs Ralph uses; call verifyTicket only from behind the worker.
3. Assert the automatic worker handles restart/resume of a queued job (lease expiry -> re-lease).
4. Assert no manual runner command is needed, no human_review status appears, and PRD passes only flips true when tickets are done.
5. Docs describe the automatic runner model (operator troubleshooting, how to disable for tests/local debugging) and no longer present per-ticket manual runner invocation as the normal path.

### Additional acceptance criteria (from 08427442)
- pnpm check includes an automatic verification loop test proving queue -> worker -> failure loop -> rerun -> done -> epic auto-PR.
- The test fails if any ticket can get stuck waiting for a human to run brain-dump verify.
- Known hazard to cover: every running Brain Dump dev server embeds a verification worker; a stale long-running dev server can lease jobs and execute OLD runner code (observed 2026-07-06: a pre-fix worker failed a run that current code passes). The worker/leasing design must prevent or surface stale-code workers.

userStories.title: Epic completion detection + automatic PR creation
acceptanceCriteria: Completing the final ticket of an epic via verification automatically produces exactly one ready PR (or flips the existing draft) with an evidence-linked body, with zero prompting
All failure modes leave a user-visible trace (comment/activity log), never a silent no-op
Toggleable via settings; pnpm check passes
userStories.description:
## Why
When the last ticket in an epic reaches done (via a certified verification pass), Brain Dump should notice and create the PR itself — no human prompting. Precedent already exists: the epic all-done trigger at src/api/tickets.ts:257-276 fires auto-learnings when every ticket in an epic hits done, and workflow start-work with autoPr:true already creates draft PRs via gh.

## Scope
1. Epic completion detection in core (not just the src/api adapter): when a runner-driven ai_verification → done transition completes, check whether every ticket in the epic is done. Hook alongside the existing auto-learnings trigger — extract the "epic just completed" detection into a shared core function both consumers use (architecture rule: shared behavior behind a core interface, no copying between adapters).
2. PR strategy on epic completion (all via execFileNoThrow + gh, never shell interpolation):
   - If the epic's work branch already has a draft PR (created by start-work autoPr): flip it to ready-for-review and rewrite the body.
   - Else: create a PR from the current branch to settings.prTargetBranch.
   - Multi-branch epics (tickets on different branches): create/ready one PR per branch; if branches are inconsistent or the working tree state is unresolvable, do NOT guess — post a needs-attention comment on the epic's newest ticket and log via log.error with a clear reason (Rule 1: no silent failures).
3. PR body: epic title + description summary, per-ticket list (title, linked commits, verification run verdict + git SHA from the sealed manifest), evidence summary counts, and a note that all tickets passed AI verification. Link the PR to all epic tickets via the existing link-pr / sync-links machinery (which already syncs PR statuses project-wide).
4. Settings: `epicAutoPr` toggle in the settings table + Settings UI (default ON). Respect existing autoCreatePr/prTargetBranch semantics; document interaction between the two.
5. Failure feedback: gh missing/unauthenticated, no remote, or push rejection → surfaced as an activity-log entry + comment (user-visible), never a silent catch. brain-dump doctor covers gh auth (see e2e ticket).
6. Guard rails: never force-push; never push to main/master directly (enforce-review-before-push semantics preserved); idempotent — re-running completion detection must not open duplicate PRs (check existing PR by branch via gh pr list first).
7. Tests: unit tests for completion detection (partial epic, already-done tickets, no epic); integration test with gh mocked at the execFile boundary covering draft-flip, fresh-create, duplicate-prevention, and failure-comment paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- Completing the final ticket of an epic via verification automatically produces exactly one ready PR (or flips the existing draft) with an evidence-linked body, with zero prompting
- All failure modes leave a user-visible trace (comment/activity log), never a silent no-op
- Toggleable via settings; pnpm check passes

userStories.title: Cross-provider workflow parity: skills, CLI, and MCP surfaces
acceptanceCriteria: A parity matrix (docs table, generated or checked by test where feasible): workflow step × provider class → how it's fulfilled (MCP action / CLI command / hook / prompt). No cell empty for the new flow.
Pi can run a full ticket lifecycle through the new flow using ONLY the brain-dump CLI
Hook-less providers cannot skip verification via MCP (precondition tests prove it)
Cross-environment test suite covers the new transitions for every provider class
userStories.description:
## Why
The new flow (ai_verification, verify runner, evidence, no human_review) must land consistently in ALL provider classes, not just Claude Code. Brain Dump has three classes of provider integration and each needs explicit parity treatment:
- **MCP providers** (claude-code, cursor, vscode, opencode, copilot-cli): share the MCP tool surface — maximize shared behavior.
- **CLI-only providers** (pi): everything the workflow needs must exist as brain-dump CLI commands.
- **Skill-using providers**: workflow skills should be consistent across providers, generated from the canonical data (sync-generator ticket), with provider-unique framing only where the provider's format genuinely requires it.

## Scope
1. **CLI parity audit**: enumerate every MCP action the new workflow uses (workflow start/complete, review submit-finding/mark-fixed/get-findings/check-complete/generate-demo, verify + verification history) and verify each has a CLI equivalent in cli/commands + command-registry. Close gaps — Pi runs the ENTIRE workflow through the CLI, so any missing command breaks Pi silently. Update .pi/prompts/*.md (via the sync generator) for the new steps.
2. **MCP-side precondition enforcement**: providers without hooks (vscode, cursor editor, opencode) rely on MCP preconditions — ensure the new transitions (ai_verification entry/exit, no submit-feedback, runner-only done) are enforced in mcp-server tools, not just documented, so hook-less environments can't drift. Extend mcp-server/tools/preconditions + cross-environment tests (mcp-server/__tests__/cross-environment.test.ts).
3. **Hook parity**: update each provider's enforcement for the new flow — .claude/hooks/*, hooks/copilot/pre-tool-use.sh, .cursor hooks (setup-cursor.sh installed), .opencode/plugins/brain-dump-review-*.ts. All hardcode state lists / marker names / tool-action names; they must learn the verification step. Codex/Pi have no hooks — confirm MCP/CLI preconditions cover them.
4. **Skill consistency experiment**: with the sync generator in place, diff the per-provider skills — document which differences are genuinely required by the provider format vs. historical accident; eliminate the accidents. Note findings in docs (interesting to see how close to identical they can get, per the epic owner).
5. **Setup scripts**: scripts/setup-*.sh and install.sh mention workflow behavior — sweep for stale references to human_review/submit-feedback.

## Acceptance criteria
- A parity matrix (docs table, generated or checked by test where feasible): workflow step × provider class → how it's fulfilled (MCP action / CLI command / hook / prompt). No cell empty for the new flow.
- Pi can run a full ticket lifecycle through the new flow using ONLY the brain-dump CLI
- Hook-less providers cannot skip verification via MCP (precondition tests prove it)
- Cross-environment test suite covers the new transitions for every provider class

userStories.title: Verification queue: idempotent enqueue and durable worker state
acceptanceCriteria: Moving a ticket into ai_verification automatically creates or refreshes one pending verification job.
Duplicate generate-demo/repair calls do not create duplicate runnable jobs.
Job state survives process restart and supports safe leasing for a single active runner.

userStories.description:
## Why
A ticket entering ai_verification must not depend on a human copying a command from the UI. Brain Dump needs a durable queue so verification work is recorded, deduplicated, leased, retried, and resumed after process restarts.

## Scope
1. Add a verification job model/table or equivalent durable state for tickets awaiting runner certification.
2. Enqueue exactly once when review.generate-demo moves a ticket to ai_verification, when repair-legacy-handoff moves a valid legacy ticket to ai_verification, and when a verification-failure repair regenerates a demo.
3. Store status: queued, running, succeeded, failed, blocked/dead, plus attempt count, nextRunAt, lastError, leasedBy, leaseExpiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt.
4. Make enqueue idempotent per ticket/current demo script so duplicate MCP/CLI calls cannot create duplicate runs.
5. Expose read APIs for UI/CLI/MCP to inspect queued/running state without allowing agents to write evidence.
6. Keep this off hot paths: enqueue is a tiny transaction; no verification execution occurs inside route loaders, MCP tool dispatch, or generate-demo itself.

## Acceptance criteria
- Moving a ticket into ai_verification automatically creates or refreshes one pending verification job.
- Duplicate generate-demo/repair calls do not create duplicate runnable jobs.
- Job state survives process restart and supports safe leasing for a single active runner.
- Tests cover enqueue idempotency, lease expiry, retry scheduling, and no blocking work in generate-demo.

userStories.title: Automatic verification worker drains ai_verification without human commands
acceptanceCriteria: A ticket moved to ai_verification is picked up automatically and receives a verification run without the user running a command.
Worker restarts do not lose queued jobs or duplicate in-flight verification runs.
Infra errors retry according to the queue policy, then block loudly instead of spinning forever.
Focused integration tests prove queue -> worker -> verifyTicket -> done/failure/block transitions.
userStories.description:
## Why
The verification gate is only useful if it runs itself. The current UI shows brain-dump verify run as a manual operator command. Replace that with a managed worker that drains queued verification jobs and calls the existing runner path automatically.

## Scope
1. Implement a background worker around core/verification.ts that claims queued verification jobs, runs verifyTicket, records the result, and releases/completes the job.
2. Start the worker automatically from Brain Dump runtime surfaces that are already running locally, with an opt-out setting/env for tests and constrained environments. Startup must be asynchronous and non-blocking.
3. Provide a CLI debugging entrypoint such as brain-dump verify worker/status, but per-ticket verification must not require user invocation.
4. Concurrency defaults to 1; no two workers may verify the same ticket concurrently.
5. Preserve existing outcome semantics: certified pass -> done; assertion fail -> loop-back; infra_error/uncertified -> blocked ai_verification with evidence/report.
6. Record telemetry/logging for queue wait time, execution time, status, attempts, and runner errors without high-cardinality aggregate labels.

## Acceptance criteria
- A ticket moved to ai_verification is picked up automatically and receives a verification run without the user running a command.
- Worker restarts do not lose queued jobs or duplicate in-flight verification runs.
- Infra errors retry according to the queue policy, then block loudly instead of spinning forever.
- Focused integration tests prove queue -> worker -> verifyTicket -> done/failure/block transitions.

userStories.title: Add verification worker operations, health checks, and recovery controls
acceptanceCriteria: A user can diagnose why ai_verification tickets are not moving without running a per-ticket verification command.
Pausing/resuming and requeue/dead-letter controls are audited and cannot certify tickets by themselves.
Doctor reports stale worker/queue conditions with concrete remediation.
Tests cover healthy, paused, stale, retrying, dead-letter, and schema-drift states.
userStories.description:
## Why
Once verification is automatic, a stalled worker becomes the new hidden human gate. Operators need a small, reliable control surface to see queue health, pause noisy execution, requeue recoverable jobs, and diagnose why tickets are not moving without editing database rows by hand.

## Scope
1. Extend brain-dump doctor/admin checks with verification worker health: worker enabled, queue depth by state, oldest queued age, stale running leases, last error, Playwright availability, app boot capability, and schema/version drift.
2. Add CLI read/control commands for verification jobs: list/status, pause/resume worker, requeue a dead/stale job, and mark an unrecoverable job dead with an audit comment.
3. Keep controls operator-only CLI/core surfaces; do not expose evidence writes or pass/fail mutation to MCP tools available to implementing agents.
4. Emit structured logs/telemetry for worker start/stop, claim, retry, stale lease recovery, dead-letter, and pause/resume without high-cardinality aggregate labels.
5. Add UI read-only visibility where useful by reusing the queue read model from the UI status ticket.
6. Add tests for doctor output, pause/resume behavior, requeue, dead-letter audit comments, and stale lease recovery.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can diagnose why ai_verification tickets are not moving without running a per-ticket verification command.
- Pausing/resuming and requeue/dead-letter controls are audited and cannot certify tickets by themselves.
- Doctor reports stale worker/queue conditions with concrete remediation.
- Tests cover healthy, paused, stale, retrying, dead-letter, and schema-drift states.

epicDescription:
Replace human review entirely with an evidence-based AI verification gate. New flow: backlog → ready → in_progress → ai_review → ai_verification → done. A deterministic runner executes machine-executable demo steps against a fresh boot of the current code, capturing tamper-evident evidence (Playwright screenshots for UI steps, real HTTP request/response captures for API steps) attributed to "{provider} ralph" (claude ralph, pi ralph, cursor ralph, ...). Verification pass → Brain Dump itself sets the ticket to done (no human approval step). Fail → verification findings are filed and the ticket loops back to implementation with failed steps + evidence injected into the next Ralph iteration, repeating until clean. Re-verification always re-runs the full step suite so fixes cannot regress previously passing steps.

Epic auto-PR: when the last ticket in an epic reaches done, Brain Dump detects epic completion and creates/readies the PR itself (via gh) with an evidence-linked body — no human prompting.

Anti-fabrication guarantees: the implementing agent only authors step specs — it cannot mark steps passed, upload evidence, or set done (no MCP action exists for any of these; only the runner transitions ai_verification → done). The runner boots the app itself on an ephemeral port, records git HEAD SHA + dirty flag + boot log in an HMAC-SHA256-sealed provenance manifest, and refuses to certify runs whose diff touches the runner itself. Exception state instead of human gate: uncertified/tripwire runs and 3 consecutive failed repair loops leave the ticket in ai_verification flagged blocked/needs-attention — nothing self-certifies past a broken runner.

Foundation-first: tickets 1-2 centralize the status/workflow-step definitions (currently duplicated across ~30 code sites) and generate provider skill/prompt files from that single source, so this step — and every future step — is cheap to add for all providers.

Full plan document: see the "AI Verification Gate" artifact (published 2026-07-04).
